key_insight: A humanoid controller can often solve new tasks by reusing skills it already has, if test-time planning can express the right contact-rich, multi-stage interactions. The paper shows that the system can improve from its own attempts and keep that improvement without retraining.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to make a humanoid robot perform unseen loco-manipulation tasks it was never explicitly trained on, while adapting online at test time instead of requiring costly retraining.
method: Use a broad pre-trained controller as the base skill set for new humanoid loco-manipulation tasks.
Evolve reward programs at test time so the controller can better match the new task through repeated self-attempts.
Retain successful adaptations, enabling continual improvement without offline retraining.
impact: This matters because it points to a practical path for deploying humanoid robots in novel real-world tasks with less task-specific training. For practitioners, it suggests more flexible robots that can adapt on the fly using existing competencies rather than starting from scratch.

paper_title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper_authors: Zhuo Lin, Sirui Xu, Liuyu Bian, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui
